harbor_p22_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_001.text: Deren reached the hearing room before its door opened in the twenty-fourth week. The early arrival annoyed him because waiting had already taken months, and now he was volunteering another half-hour. His independent clerk came at the agreed time and found him staring at the hinge. She asked whether he wanted the notice read again. He said no, then yes. The room smelled of lamp oil and washed floorboards. Somewhere inside, a chair scraped once. He imagined Yan hearing the same sound from another corridor and hated that he still worried about his friend's morning.

harbor_p22_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_002.text: Yan arrived separately with the inspection sources the officer had requested. Bo had covered the ordinary crew handover under the assigned lead, and the kit count was complete. The foreman checked that fact twice in his head before catching himself. Today's hearing could not be escaped by improving a pencil inventory somewhere else. He stood outside the other door until the clerk called him. Sui came behind him carrying only her own relevant records. She looked at his clenched hands and said she had slept badly too. The admission made neither of them sleepier or less afraid.

harbor_p22_003.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p22_003.text: Answer what they ask and say when memory differs from the record. I am reminding myself as much as you. Do not volunteer my explanation of your check, and I will not borrow yours for my notice. We worked in the same system; that does not mean we knew the same things at the same time. Afterward there will still be a quay, a crew and whatever the finding requires us to do. Right now there is this room. We can enter it without deciding beforehand which version makes us most tolerable to our friends.

harbor_p22_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_004.text: The reviewer began with Deren's accident sequence. A working platform had failed beneath him after its visible patch obscured rot that the ordinary inspection routine did not reveal. The rescue had brought him out through trained crew work and prescribed care, not a miracle whose success erased the failing structure. Deren described where he stood and what he felt through the boards. He did not remember every shouted instruction. The clerk kept the uncertain interval uncertain. When the officer asked about the last patch he saw before failure, he pointed to the copied image and named only what he recognized.

harbor_p22_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_005.text: The maintenance keeper's source showed the patch had been treated as surface repair while the supporting timber remained insufficiently examined. An earlier concern about softness had entered one task note but not the use clearance where the crew looked. The keeper admitted that transfer failure. The examiner compared the rot's extent with the required inspection, explaining why the paint could not support the clearance it received. Yan listened with his eyes on the source, not Deren's face. He had wanted to believe the painted patch meant somebody else had already looked beneath it. His check had relied on that belief.

harbor_p22_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_006.text: The reviewer asked Yan what his assigned pre-use duty required. He described the surface and support check, then admitted he had accepted the recorded repair without verifying the concealed support at that location. The officer asked whether his routine would have found the concern if the task note had reached the use sheet. Probably, he said, and then corrected himself: he could not prove what he would have done in an unmade morning. He could say the actual warning would have required stopping use for the proper examination. Deren heard the correction and felt both respect and a fresh hurt.

harbor_p22_007.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p22_007.text: I missed the part of the check that asked me to verify the support rather than admire a repaired surface. The maintenance source gave me a reason to think it had been examined, but my own duty did not end there. I do not remember seeing the softness note before use. I supplied the sheet I actually had. If the finding says that gap mattered too, I will answer for the part assigned to me. I cannot tell Deren that my good intention kept him safer. He was standing on the board, and the board failed.

harbor_p22_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_008.text: The room held a silence nobody tried to improve. Deren had wanted an admission and now disliked its plainness. An apology could have let him respond generously; this account asked him to sit with the fact. The officer moved to the duty dates in Sui's remit. The captain's system required the maintenance concern to reach the use clearance through the identified receiving route. Her notice arrangement had not included an acknowledgment when a concern moved between the two books. She had reviewed completed entries and missed the source. The failure belonged to her supervision, not every act on the quay.

harbor_p22_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_009.text: Sui explained the check she performed and where it stopped. The officer asked why an unanswered transfer was not visible in the next review. She said the routine showed completed repairs more readily than unresolved technical concerns. That described the arrangement; it did not excuse her duty to examine its gaps. Her reputation had depended on decisive closure. She did not say this at the hearing because reputation was not the source requested. She supplied the dates, the missing acknowledgment and the correction. Her face felt hot when Deren's clerk asked whether that correction could have been made earlier.

harbor_p22_010.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p22_010.text: Yes, the receiving acknowledgment could have been required before this accident. I did not require it then. I can describe why the routine appeared to work and how that judgment was wrong, but neither description makes the change newly possible only after Deren was hurt. The current correction has a named receiving person and unresolved entries visible at review. The officer can examine whether it is adequate. I do not ask Deren to call the improvement payment for his pain. His claim has its own supported answer, and my work has its own consequences.

harbor_p22_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_011.text: The maintenance keeper challenged a proposed inference that he personally had seen all the rot before painting. The sources established a reported softness concern and inadequate examination, not his full knowledge of the concealed decay. The reviewer narrowed the wording while retaining the missed duty. Yan felt the room's anger shift toward the correction. He understood now how easily accuracy could look merciful to someone already responsible. Deren's clerk asked the examiner to explain the distinction in ordinary words. The examiner did. The resulting account was more specific and no less serious about a man falling through a working platform.

harbor_p22_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_012.text: The lost-work assessment identified thirteen scheduled half-days that Deren could not perform in the supported interval, at the actual two-copper rate. Twenty-six was due from the port employer's liability line under the board's current authorization. It was separate from earned voyage wages already paid and from prescribed care previously supported. Compatible stock work later performed remained its own ordinary income. The reviewer compared the roster, care restrictions and payment sources before naming the twenty-six. Deren gripped the chair seat. He had carried the amount through so many mornings that hearing it aloud felt almost like losing it.

harbor_p22_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_013.text: His clerk asked whether receiving the twenty-six would close every possible injury question. The notice explained the scope and remaining review route for any other supported claim; it did not demand an unlimited release to pay the lost earnings. Deren heard the words twice. He said he wanted the money paid and wanted the copy kept where he could read it with help. The receiving office arranged both. Sui did not offer her private purse. Yan did not offer to deduct the amount from his own wage in a gesture. The employer source could answer without turning payment into charity.

harbor_p22_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_014.text: The final accountability result assigned the supported failures to maintenance transmission, Yan's pre-use verification and Sui's unresolved-notice supervision. The competent port authority required documented retraining, a revised check with independent comparison and bounded removal from specified unsupervised inspection duties until the review conditions were met. The ordinary employment and technical roles remained with their actual keepers. Nobody declared every worker unfit or abolished the port because one platform failed. The consequences were specific enough to change who could sign the next use clearance. Yan felt their practical weight more sharply than he would have felt a speech about shame.

harbor_p22_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_015.text: Sui's supervisory review required the unresolved maintenance queue to be examined at stated intervals by the proper second officer, with acknowledgment gaps visible before use. She would continue ordinary captain duties within that result, subject to the named follow-up. The authority did not ask her to supervise her own compliance alone. She signed receipt of the decision and asked for the first review date. Her hand shook once, an irritation she wanted to hide. The clerk waited without commenting. A captain could be seen receiving a consequence without immediately making a better public sentence about it.

harbor_p22_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_016.text: The office paid Deren's twenty-six after the authorized source and receipt were confirmed. The coins came in an cloth pouch supplied for the payment, which he emptied into his own purse and returned if the keeper required it. He had expected the weight to feel immense. It felt like money. Rent, food and a small old debt had already named places for it. He thanked the payment clerk because she had explained the receipt clearly. Then he left the room before thanking anyone else. The board's supported result did not oblige him to comfort the people whose duties had failed.

harbor_p22_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_017.text: Yan stood outside the other exit and saw Deren crossing the courtyard. He wanted to call his name. Sui put no hand on his sleeve and offered no instruction about friendship. The foreman stayed where he was until Deren looked over. Their eyes met briefly. Deren nodded once and kept walking with the independent clerk. Yan accepted the small acknowledgment as exactly that, rather than invent a pardon. The captain asked whether he had a safe way home. He did. They walked together to the road and separated there, each carrying a decision that would still exist tomorrow.

harbor_p22_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_018.text: Yue had attended the public explanation during her scheduled half-day, with only the source role she actually held. She had not seen the pre-accident check and did not become its missing witness because she helped afterward. At the contact room, Han asked whether she wanted tea. Yue said yes and then told her she had expected the finding to feel better. The clerk said Deren had received twenty-six and a supported answer; that mattered. Yue agreed. The ordinary room stayed quiet around them. They could be glad for a concrete payment without making the whole afternoon pleasing.

harbor_p22_019.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p22_019.text: I do not know what he will say to Yan. I am not going to ask him while he is counting money that has been missing for months. If he wants help reading the next route, I will give it. If he wants soup and no conversation, somebody at the stall can provide that too. We have done a piece of work today. Let us keep its size honest long enough for him to live inside the result. I know you are already imagining how the crew feels tomorrow. Tomorrow has its own kettle, and this one needs filling.

harbor_p22_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_020.text: Deren went first to pay the rent portion he had postponed under an agreed extension. The landlord received it and gave the actual receipt, without describing patience as a personal favor that erased the debt's embarrassment. Deren bought food and settled the small old obligation next. He kept a little money for himself. At the tool stall he almost bought something unnecessary simply to prove the payment was his. Then he purchased a cup to replace the chipped one he had complained about for weeks. The choice was small, useful and nobody else's business until he chose to show it.

harbor_p22_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_021.text: Bo met him at the canteen and stared at the new cup. He asked whether compensation usually improved pottery. Deren said it improved one particular vessel whose previous rim had been trying to injure his lip. The boy laughed, then asked about the finding. Deren gave the public answer and kept the private parts of his hearing where they belonged. He wanted company, not another reader explaining how fortunate he should feel. Bo complied badly for five minutes, then well enough for the rest of the meal. They argued about the canteen's turnips and the cup's excessive dignity.

harbor_p22_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_022.text: Yan spent the next morning on the rigging role he could still perform, while the specified inspection signoff belonged to its assigned independent cover. A crew member asked whether this meant the foreman had been demoted from being right. Yan said it meant a particular duty needed the result's check before he resumed it unsupervised. The man nodded and went back to the rope. Nobody needed a theatrical explanation at every load. Bo followed the actual handover and did not make a joke until the crew stood clear. Then he asked whether supervised wisdom cost extra. Yan groaned and laughed.

harbor_p22_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_023.text: Sui met the second officer at the first notice comparison. They found one concern awaiting a technical reply and kept it visible with a receiving person and date. It was not another dramatic failure, simply work that would previously have been easier to lose beneath pages. The officer asked her to stop answering his questions before he finished them. She apologized and waited. Their relationship would take practice. The captain had spent years sounding certain enough to make other people move; now part of the task required listening long enough to hear what did not yet belong in her answer.

harbor_p22_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_024.text: At home she read her son's oven letter again and wrote nothing for an hour. She did not want to send a confession he had to absolve. Finally she said the port review had reached a result, she had duties to change and she was sad about a worker's injury. Then she asked how the next bread order went. The ordinary question felt almost disrespectful beside the finding until she remembered her son was allowed a life beyond interpreting his mother's conscience. She mailed the letter through her private route and baked an uneven loaf for supper.

harbor_p22_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_025.text: The maintenance keeper began the comparison training with the technical officer. He disliked being taught beside a younger worker who could see his old signatures. The officer used examples and required the unresolved source to reach the active use sheet before a clearance could rely on it. The keeper completed the first exercise wrongly, then corrected it with the source visible. Nobody applauded his humility. A future platform needed a sound answer, and the exercise had a practical pass condition. He stayed until the check was complete, then went home tired enough not to argue with his wife about supper.

harbor_p22_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_026.text: At the warehouse, Bao's separate lost-work decision followed its own received roster and care sources. The supported amount was eighteen from the responsible warehouse employer's injury-liability account, authorized through the competent process, not Hao's closed storage-loss custody. Prescribed care continued under its proper source. Bao received the eighteen with the actual scope and further route explained. The family had expected the number to cure more worry than it could. It paid ordinary needs that had accumulated while she coughed. Her cousin helped read the receipt and asked whether she wanted to go home before deciding what gratitude sounded like.

harbor_p22_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_027.text: Bao did. At home she put part toward the agreed household expense and kept part while considering the next work. Dai's small net tasks remained offers, not a permanent income guaranteed by their friendship. The warehouse might offer a different compatible role after care clearance; Bao did not have to accept because its owner had paid a supported claim. She said this plainly to her cousin and felt suddenly defiant. Her cousin said she had known all along. Bao laughed. Recovering choice sometimes meant telling a truth aloud to someone who had already been waiting for her to believe it.

harbor_p22_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_028.text: He Ming's first regular batch reached acceptance under the ninety-six agreement after Ke completed her fourth paid half-day. The buyer's authorized substitute checked the work and paid the forty-eight balance. Forty completed the four workers' remaining wages at ten each, making twelve each altogether; the earned eight margin entered the partnership's own reserve by their agreed decision. Materials twenty-four, space sixteen, wages forty-eight and margin eight closed the batch's ninety-six. Nothing from the next three guaranteed batches was spent early. Ke counted her wage, then asked when the next real offered hours began. The table had an actual answer now.

harbor_p22_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_029.text: The partners kept the eight reserve inside the venture instead of distributing it privately. Its purpose was replacement material and business needs, with any use agreed under their own terms. An argued for buying a better lamp. Zhou preferred waiting until an evening job required one. He Ming wanted a cushion after losing stock twice. Ke did not control the partners' reserve as an employee and could still ask how future wages were protected. They discussed the next batch's source and payment sequence. Their growing business had room for disagreement without making the worker's security depend on liking the founders.

harbor_p22_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_030.text: Deren met Yan three days after the hearing, by asking the canteen keeper to pass an invitation when the foreman came for supper. The invitation named no subject. Yan arrived too early and found Deren already seated with the new cup. Neither greeted the other with a joke. The foreman sat. Deren said he had paid rent and an old debt. Yan said he was glad. Then Deren told him the amount had been present in every week of waiting, even when they spoke about Bo's handwriting. Yan looked at the cup and said he had not understood how often.

harbor_p22_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_031.text: The silence lasted until the keeper brought soup. Deren said he was angry at the missed check and angry that friendship made him feel responsible for Yan's shame. Yan answered that he did not want him to carry it. Deren laughed sharply: wanting did not remove the habit. The foreman accepted the rebuke. He asked whether the invitation meant they could remain friends while Deren stayed angry. Deren said he would not have sent it otherwise. Both men ate. The soup was too salty, and neither complained until the harder sentence had settled on the table.

harbor_p22_032.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p22_032.text: I am grateful you asked me here. I do not know how to make this less awkward without pretending you have finished feeling something you have not. I can answer if you ask about the finding. I can also leave it alone when you want supper. Next week my ordinary rigging shift ends later, but I can meet on the rest evening if you choose. Do not agree now because I look miserable. You are entitled to send an invitation when you actually want me at the table, and I am entitled to hope another one comes.

harbor_p22_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_033.text: Deren said the next invitation would require a better joke. Yan offered Bo's latest accusation that supervised wisdom cost extra. Deren groaned. The foreman said this was the available stock and customers seeking quality should shop elsewhere. Their laughter came cautiously, then with genuine relief. It did not reduce the twenty-six or alter the finding. For the first time since the hearing, Deren could imagine keeping the claim and the friend in the same room without constantly arranging a protective cloth between them. He told Yan the new cup cost too much. The foreman admired it anyway.

harbor_p22_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_034.text: On the safe road afterward, Yan passed the platform's repaired successor from beyond its use boundary. The sound new boards had been checked by the assigned independent authority. He would not sign their inspection alone until the result's conditions were met. A crew used the structure under the clearance, moving slowly with a load. He watched without trying to find proof that his old judgment had been reasonable. Then he went home. His mother asked why he looked lighter and still tired. He said he had eaten supper with Deren. She smiled and put no further question on his plate.

harbor_p22_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_035.text: Bao's supervisor received the door-duty result. It required the reported concerns to enter the maintenance route with acknowledgment, and a retraining and signoff arrangement before he resumed that responsibility. He argued that oral complaints arrived constantly. The officer asked how the current routine distinguished inconvenience from a fault affecting exit. He had no answer. That gap belonged in the result. Bao read the explanation with her cousin and said she hoped the next worker would not have to write beautifully to be heard. The cousin said the new route should be tested by speech, as Bao had chosen to do.

harbor_p22_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_036.text: Hao paid another sixteen from the private building account for the approved final fittings inside the confirmed smaller footprint. Gross sources remained one hundred thirty-six, spending became one hundred twenty, and the sixteen balance returned to her repair deposit after that contract closed. The storage-loss account had already closed at sixty-four paid and sixteen returned to trading. Bao's eighteen injury payment belonged to the separate employer liability source. The warehouse could now reopen its cleared sections under the actual building and operating checks. Hao's steward disliked the smaller rent roll and admitted the doorway was better than before.

harbor_p22_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_037.text: The cloth trader's daughter placed their recovered stock in the private space she had arranged and bought a small new batch with their business money. Her father still wanted the lost resale margin argued to its last possible copper. She did not forbid the review route. She asked who would handle sales while he pursued it. He said she could. She said she could, and wanted him to decide whether the remaining question deserved all his present hours. He frowned, then went to open the shop. The claim's availability did not require the family to live forever at its doorway.

harbor_p22_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_038.text: Miao visited the restarted shop with the partnership's quote information. The trader listened without reopening the old exclusivity argument. The daughter asked the dates and said she would return when a batch suited. Miao gave no priority promise. Afterward he told Yue he had finally learned that a customer could remember a refused offer without becoming an enemy in every future conversation. She asked whether this was a new insight or evidence he had run out of customers to offend. He laughed and admitted both might be possible. They bought ordinary tea and watched people bargain badly across the lane.

harbor_p22_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_039.text: Fen's apprenticeship review found her careful and slow. The aunt said the pace was appropriate for now and named the next skill. Fen wanted another adjective, preferably brilliant. Aning heard the disappointment and laughed until the aunt asked her whether her own explanations had grown more patient. They both blushed. After work they practiced reading a difficult line aloud to one another, taking turns as the impatient customer. Fen's imitation of a merchant sigh was so exact that Aning nearly spilled the kettle. The arithmetic improved less than their mood. Both gains seemed useful when they returned the next morning.

harbor_p22_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_040.text: Luo's care review allowed consideration of sustained light sorting under the Reed Steps schedule, with rest intervals and limits still specified. Travel could be planned ordinarily; heavy saw or load tasks remained excluded. He took the answer to the employer's receiving route and asked for those limits in the work terms. He did not buy a ticket on the first good sentence. Fen read the reply when it arrived and said she could now be afraid of something specific rather than a place swallowing him. Luo answered that specific fear was still fear. She said she knew and preferred it.

harbor_p22_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_041.text: The employer page matched the light role and bounded term. Luo intended to begin after the harbor's final season checks, with private travel and permitted contact. Fen had her apprenticeship and room arrangement to consider; she would not accompany him by default. They planned which household objects stayed and which belonged to each person. His fishing things could leave the shelf when he did. Her learning pages could remain. The discussion felt unbearably practical until he said the old room had held them through a difficult stretch. It did not have to hold both forever to remain a good place.

harbor_p22_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_042.text: He Ming received Jun's update: their mother was moving more comfortably within the care plan and had begun complaining that neighbors visited when she wanted a nap. The message relieved her enough to laugh. She wrote about the new larger room and Ke's completed trial, then described the birthday goat instead of making every paragraph a financial proof. Jun had asked for a story. She gave him one with no useful advice inside it. The ordinary private correspondence would continue under their agreed contact, imperfectly and in real time, without either sibling claiming silence meant the other had vanished again.

harbor_p22_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_043.text: At the partnership, Ke accepted the next paid offer under the guaranteed schedule after the first batch closed. She had liked the work and disliked the founders' occasional habit of finishing an explanation among themselves while the employee still waited for its point. He Ming asked her to say which instruction did that. Ke showed the source. Zhou corrected it without pretending the question was an attack on solidarity. An said the gull had been guilty of similar obscurity for months. Ke said its job did not involve readable instructions. They laughed and put the clear page beside the tools.

harbor_p22_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_044.text: The eight earned margin stayed in the venture's reserve under the partners' agreement. They chose to buy two copper of tying stock only when the next job's needs made the purpose clear. Six remained. The purchase was private business money, not a deduction from Ke's next wage or a call on emergency readiness. An proposed finally dividing the remaining six to celebrate. Zhou asked whether he preferred two copper now or replacement stock later. He said the question's phrasing was biased. He Ming agreed, and they kept the reserve after discussing the risks without treating frugality as a personality virtue.

harbor_p22_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_045.text: Wu finished the canteen's stock check and came to collect the food the partnership had ordered. She found the partners arguing about the reserve and said the duck would spend all six on a bath. Ke asked whether the bird had a wage. Wu said it had acquired a household subsidy by threatening morale. The workers laughed. The food arrived at its private price and the agreed bowls went to the people who had ordered them. Wu returned to her children with her schedule intact. The partnership could be one of her circles without buying every hour in her life.

harbor_p22_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_046.text: Han began a new private painting board with no customer waiting. After the paid signs, she wanted a curve nobody could reject for commercial reasons. She ruined the first one and blamed the lack of an invoice. Duan told her to stop inventing employers for leisure. Han laughed and kept working. Yue waited outside the ordinary safe painting area, listening to the dog complain from the place its keeper had assigned. When the clerk finished, they walked home with the board wrapped in Han's own cloth. It was her property, her disappointment and her private pleasure to continue.

harbor_p22_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_047.text: At the wage desk, another new household question required an interpreter for a future ordinary receiving hour. The office's own staffing route would handle that request; Yue's remaining twelve interpretation copper was not automatically a fund for every person who arrived. Han identified the actual referral and receiving keeper. Yue's scheduled comparison checked that the public room and hour matched. She had grown better at leaving work with its competent owner rather than searching for a reason every gap required her remaining term. The clerk noticed and teased her privately that she was becoming less employable as a heroic institution.

harbor_p22_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_048.text: Yue said heroic institutions paid badly in sleep. Han asked whether the southern guard trial would have paid better. The date had already passed; Yue had declined that timing and received no commission. They laughed without reopening the decision. The next road would begin with ordinary local questions, not a job awarded by destiny for finishing a harbor inquiry. Yue had done that before and could do it again. She practiced briefly the next morning on the familiar dry strip, forming only the earned pairs, moving the marker within its known range and releasing them before strain blurred the finish.

harbor_p22_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_049.text: The clerk's four-copper decision copying task received operations approval before the pages were ordered. It used Yue's appointment copying line for the permitted result explanation and receiving routes. The term's copying total rose from six to ten. Private care details stayed outside the public summary. Deren received his own explained copy, while the ordinary crew could see the duty changes relevant to them. Yue completed the second scheduled half-day comparing those routes. She wanted the paper to last longer than her presence at the desk. The named ordinary keepers, rather than a visitor's private notes, would carry the next questions.

harbor_p22_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_050.text: Qin read the public duty result after work and asked Han whether Deren wanted his company. She told him to ask through the ordinary permitted route rather than make the injured man host everyone's relief. Qin wrote an invitation with no demand for an answer. Deren eventually chose tea at the stall, where the old man brought no account book. They discussed beans, a song and the new cup. Deren admitted he had expected elders to make compensation sound like a lesson. Qin said lessons were tiring after supper and offered an absurdly incorrect line of the song instead.

harbor_p22_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_051.text: The replacement custodian continued covering actual intervals when Qin took a private rest afternoon. Neither man described the arrangement as proof the old keeper should retire immediately or never retire. Qin had begun considering a shorter future role under ordinary work terms, with his employer's needs and his own income still to be discussed. He told Yue this as a possibility, not a plan she needed to secure before leaving. She asked what he would do with free mornings. He said the beans were already negotiating for more attention. The garden remained unprofitable enough to keep its moral authority weak.

harbor_p22_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_052.text: Sui's next supervisory comparison found the revised receiving acknowledgment working on a maintenance concern. The second officer signed his own check and identified the next review. The captain did not declare the whole port corrected forever. She had a finite result to carry through duties. That evening she met Yan after his covered inspection interval and asked whether he was sleeping. A little, he said. She admitted the same. They discussed their next work rather than trade apologies to make the hearing smaller. The tide rose beside a quay whose people now knew more precisely where its checks had failed.

harbor_p22_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_053.text: Yan told Sui he had eaten with Deren. She smiled and asked whether he wanted to say more. He did not. She accepted the private boundary, which relieved him. The captain had enough public information to do her own job without possessing the friendship's whole conversation. They walked to the ordinary road fork and went home separately. The foreman's mother had saved a bowl. Sui's loaf was uneven again. Neither supper proved accountability complete; both belonged to people continuing after a hard answer, whose lives contained appetite and small irritations alongside the next review date.

harbor_p22_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_054.text: Yue received four copper for the week's two completed half-days, and six paid the agreed bed and meals. Twenty-four half-days had now been paid in the new term. With four approved copying copper, spending reached one hundred forty-two and unspent fifty-eight: wages eight, bed twelve, ferry eighteen, copies eight, interpretation twelve. The emergency reserve remained one hundred seventy-two spent and sixty-eight unspent, with four unused stones. Deren's twenty-six and Bao's eighteen came from their respective employers' proper liability sources, never those balances. Yue checked the figures once and put the account away before Han arrived for their planned walk.

harbor_p22_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_055.text: They went to the shore wall carrying privately bought buns. Han asked what Yue had feared most at the hearing. The traveler said she had feared a correct answer would still leave people unable to speak. The clerk said perhaps some needed silence first. Yue agreed. They stood watching ordinary boats under the open route, then disputed the buns' filling with much greater certainty. The wind lifted Han's scarf, and Yue caught its loose end with an ordinary hand before it reached the water. The clerk thanked her and said this was the useful cultivation skill she preferred.

harbor_p22_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_056.text: Yue protested that no qi had been involved. Han said she had seen the result and was uninterested in the marketing. They laughed. The humor felt freer now that their departure conversation had no hidden promise waiting beneath it. There would still be sadness, ordinary letters and missed evenings. For now the buns were warm and the shore road clear. Yue gave the scarf end back, leaving the garment Han's. A small object caught in time could brighten a walk without becoming evidence that the traveler should stay forever to intercept every future thing the wind might take.

harbor_p22_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_057.text: He Ming found the new room's kettle lid rattling and accused An of buying a musical instrument instead of kitchenware. He said the kettle had been supplied with the rented room and demanded the landlord be reviewed for excessive talent. Zhou folded a cloth beneath the handle where the maker allowed it, quieting the lid. Ke applauded until the kettle began again. They abandoned dignity and laughed. The next batch's materials were ordered under its actual advance; lunch waited on the stove. He Ming touched the ugly gull's board and told it the orchestra required a conductor.

harbor_p22_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p22_058.text: At the end of the twenty-fourth week, Deren washed his new cup and set it beside the repaired stock table. Tomorrow's compatible work had its ordinary hours. The finding had paid supported lost earnings and changed actual duties; his ankle still required care, and friendship still required honesty. He looked at the chair whose wobble no longer disturbed him and sat down. Outside, Bo's voice called a joke through the doorway. Deren answered that the joke needed an independent review. The boy laughed, and the ordinary room held them both without demanding either make the afternoon's hard truth disappear.
